channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Water
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] CISA lists the BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day as exploited; a suspected China-nexus espionage group has used it since late August
item.category: Top Story
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-102764 in BeyondTrust Remote Support to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 16 October, with a 19 October deadline for federal agencies. A day earlier, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reported that a suspected China-nexus espionage group it tracks as ARMORY CASTLE (formerly UNC5221) had exploited the flaw, rated CVSS v4.0 9.3, as a zero-day since late August. The intruders gained root on Remote Support appliances, harvested credentials, deleted logs and used the tool’s file transfer to take documents. BeyondTrust shipped a fix on 8 October; self-hosted appliances without automatic updates must be patched by hand. GTIG names no victims or sectors, and no water utility has reported a compromise. It leads this edition because it is the newest confirmed exploitation of a remote-access tool by a suspected state-linked group, and in our assessment remote-support tools are a common way integrators and SCADA vendors reach utility workstations. No attack on water control systems has been confirmed in the past 30 days. - CISA KEV, 16 Oct 2026 (catalog of 21 Oct 2026); Google Threat Intelligence Group, 15 Oct 2026 (primary); BeyondTrust advisory BT26-05; SecurityWeek, 16 Oct 2026 - Exploitation from late Aug 2026; fix 8 Oct 2026; disclosed 15 Oct 2026; KEV 16 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Attackers took over internet-reachable refrigeration controllers at about 700 French supermarkets; France’s cyber agency says the campaign is probably still running
item.category: Incident — Cross-sector OT attack on remotely managed controllers (food retail, France); confirmed by French authorities
item.description: Over the nights of 11–13 October, attackers remotely changed settings on web-managed refrigeration controllers in French supermarkets, forcing long or continuous defrost cycles that delayed alarms and pushed some cases to around 50 °C. Finance Minister Roland Lescure told Parliament on 13 October that about 700 stores were hit, at chains including Carrefour, Coopérative U, E.Leclerc, Intermarché/Netto and Monoprix; the Paris prosecutor has reported fires, and its cybercrime section has opened an inquiry. CERT-FR’s alert named Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers on 12 October, added Copeland and Dixell xweb units on 13 October, and says in its 16 October update that the campaigns are probably still ongoing; no new attack nights have been reported since 13 October, and the alert had not been revised again as of 23 October. No group has claimed it, no ransom was demanded and the entry route has not been established; Danfoss says most affected units are end-of-life. Les Mousquetaires, which runs Intermarché and Netto, has said the intrusion came through a company that maintained refrigeration at some of its stores; that is the retailer’s statement, not an official finding. No water system is involved. In our assessment the method, remote setpoint changes on controllers left reachable from the internet, mirrors this year’s attacks on US water systems, and Nozomi’s 13 October analysis ties the same exposed-access weakness to them. - CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012, 12 Oct 2026, updated 13 and 16 Oct 2026 (primary); Finance Minister’s figure via AP, 13 Oct 2026; SecurityWeek, 15 Oct 2026; Les Mousquetaires statement via Dark Reading; Nozomi Networks analysis, 13 Oct 2026 - Attacks 11–13 Oct 2026; latest CERT-FR update 16 Oct 2026, no later version as of 23 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Symantec: a China-nexus Warlock ransomware crew breached a water utility through on-premises SharePoint
item.category: Incident — Ransomware intrusion at a water utility (IT-side), vendor-reported
item.description: Symantec’s threat hunters reported on 1 October that a China-nexus threat actor it calls Longlegs (also tracked as Storm-2603) attacked at least four organizations in the past two months: a water utility, a telecom provider, a regional government body and a university, in Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries across Europe, Africa and Latin America. None is named. The group typically gets in by exploiting on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server; the only CVEs Symantec names are the 2025 “ToolShell” flaws, plus related SharePoint bugs. It then uses a vulnerable signed driver to switch off security tools, a Visual Studio Code tunnel for persistence and the domain SYSVOL share to push ransomware. In Symantec’s detailed case study, an intrusion at an unnamed critical-infrastructure organization, Warlock reached at least 33 hosts; the report does not say whether that victim was the water utility, and it describes no OT or operational impact. In our assessment, a domain-wide ransomware push is exactly where a flat or over-trusted link between utility IT and SCADA turns an office outage into an operations problem. - Symantec / Carbon Black Threat Hunter Team report, 1 Oct 2026 (primary); BleepingComputer and SecurityWeek coverage - Intrusions over the previous two months; published 1 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] FBI and Secret Service: the FortiBleed campaign against Fortinet firewalls is still active, and their warning covers the water sector
item.category: Incident — Active credential-theft campaign against Fortinet firewalls and VPNs; FBI and Secret Service warning
item.description: In a joint advisory dated 6 October, the FBI and US Secret Service said the FortiBleed campaign against internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways remains an active threat. There is no CVE: the attackers log in with reused or leaked credentials, crack passwords stored with legacy SHA-256 hashing and sniff authentication traffic. Once in, they create their own administrator accounts and sometimes reset or delete the originals, locking owners out, and the access is resold; the advisory says brokers have passed it to INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates, and SOCRadar says it has confirmed at least 12 ransomware deployments. The advisory covers all 16 US critical-infrastructure sectors and names water and wastewater among them; no water utility or control-system compromise has been described. SOCRadar’s count of 86,644 working device credentials in 194 countries dates from 19 June and is not a new figure. FortiGates often sit at a utility’s IT/OT boundary or carry vendor VPN access (editorial assessment). - FBI and US Secret Service joint advisory JCSA-20261006-01, 6 Oct 2026 (primary); The Hacker News and Cybersecurity Dive, 7 Oct 2026 - Advisory 6 Oct 2026; credential count dated 19 Jun 2026

item.title: [Low] Vicksburg, Mississippi ransomware takes city systems offline and disrupts utility bill payments
item.category: Incident — Municipal ransomware disrupts utility bill payments; no OT impact reported
item.description: Vicksburg Mayor Willis Thompson said in a statement on 1 October that a ransomware attack forced the city to take systems offline temporarily, disrupting its utility payment systems; emergency services were not affected. He said no one’s service will be cut off and no late-payment penalties will be charged while the investigation runs, and that the city is still working out whether personal or confidential information was compromised. The FBI, DHS, state officials and private responders are helping. No group has claimed the attack, and the city has not commented on any ransom demand. The reporting does not say which utility services the billing covers, and nothing points to water or wastewater control systems being affected. It is an IT-side incident, but municipal utilities that share city IT, billing and accounts should know what a city-wide shutdown would take down with it (editorial assessment). - Mayor’s statement, 1 Oct 2026, reported by The Record - Confirmed 1 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] After France’s supermarket attacks, Forescout counts nearly 13,000 exposed refrigeration control services worldwide, and Waterfall sets out a minimum firewall checklist for small sites
item.category: Research — Internet exposure of remotely managed controllers after the French attacks; firewall guidance for small sites
item.description: Forescout’s Vedere Labs reported on 22 October that internet searches for ten refrigeration-controller product families returned 12,976 exposed service observations on 6,017 public IP addresses in 99 countries and territories; it counts services, not devices. About 80% of the Danfoss StoreView observations ran firmware older than 4.3.1, which carries known flaws, and Forescout counts more than 20 hacktivist claims of attacks on refrigeration systems since January, mostly in Spain and Italy (claims, not confirmed incidents). It says the entry route, actor and persistence in the French attacks are still unknown. Two days earlier, Waterfall Security’s Andrew Ginter, noting that the attacks look similar to recent ones on small US water utilities, set out a minimum setup for sites with little IT staff: a commercial-grade firewall with VPN, MFA and automatic updates; deny all traffic by default and allow only fixed addresses such as the service provider’s office, never home or mobile ones; back up and document the configuration; and replace the firewall about every four years. His theories about how the French attackers got in are his own and unconfirmed. - Forescout Vedere Labs, 22 Oct 2026 (primary); Waterfall Security, 20 Oct 2026; Industrial Cyber, 23 Oct 2026 - Published 20 and 22 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] MITRE ATT&CK v20 catalogues the July attacks on more than 30 Minnesota water utilities as campaign C0066
item.category: Research — MITRE ATT&CK v20 documents the 2026 US water-utility PLC campaign
item.description: MITRE’s ATT&CK v20, announced this week, adds campaign C0066, “2026 U.S. Water Utilities Attacks” (entry created 8 October, last modified 13 October). It covers intrusions from 27 July at more than 30 municipal water and wastewater utilities in Minnesota, part of wider activity the FBI and EPA reported in at least seven states. The attackers reached internet-facing Rockwell/Allen-Bradley MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 PLCs through cellular gateways at water towers and sewer lift stations and changed their IP addresses and passwords to lock operators out. At least one victim’s program logic was altered, and reported effects included loss of water pressure, flooding and one treatment plant taken offline. MITRE says the campaign has not been formally attributed. The release also adds CyberAv3ngers’ IOControl malware, a Mexican campaign (C0064) that reached a municipal water utility, and a new ICS scripting technique, T1701. C0066’s technique list, from default credentials to modified parameters and program logic, is a ready-made checklist for detection and tabletop work. - MITRE ATT&CK campaign C0066, created 8 Oct 2026, modified 13 Oct 2026 (primary); Industrial Cyber, 16 Oct 2026 - Campaign activity from 27 Jul 2026; entry last modified 13 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] CISA and FBI warn operators to tighten control of ICS integrators’ access
item.category: Guidance — CISA/FBI on third-party ICS integrators
item.description: CISA and the FBI released a fact sheet on 24 September on the risks of working with third-party industrial control system integrators. It draws on an FBI analysis of a 2025 intrusion at a US automation firm serving power utilities and transportation customers, in which actors searched for SCADA and customer records and staged nine archives holding about 800 files of network schematics, device configurations and customer details. Water is not among the named sectors, but small utilities that rely on one integrator for PLC and SCADA work share the same exposure. The agencies recommend least-privilege access, cybersecurity terms in contracts, monitored on-demand remote access, and disconnecting devices from the public internet. - CISA and FBI fact sheet, 24 Sep 2026 (primary); Industrial Cyber and SecurityWeek coverage - Fact sheet published 24 Sep 2026; underlying intrusion Mar–Apr 2025

item.title: [Critical] Ivanti Connect Secure: a three-flaw chain gave attackers root on fully patched VPNs, and one link is still unpatched
item.category: Advisory — Exploited VPN flaw chain, CISA KEV; one link still unpatched; remote-access edge
item.description: Ivanti disclosed on 13 October that attackers chained three flaws to run commands as root on fully patched Connect Secure VPN appliances at a limited number of customers. Two of the flaws are fixed under a single CVE, CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS v3.1 8.6), an authentication bypass that leads to unauthenticated command execution; the third, a privilege-escalation bug, has no CVE and no patch yet, with a fix promised in the coming weeks; no public fix or CVE for it had appeared as of 23 October. Volexity, which found the chain during an incident response, tracks the actor as a new group, UTA0576; Volexity and Defused date exploitation to at least early October (1–3 October). The intruders left no web shell; they stole domain credentials, queried Active Directory for LAPS passwords and BitLocker keys, sprayed passwords and wiped logs. CISA added the CVE to KEV on 13 October with a 16 October deadline and warns that Ivanti’s Integrity Checker may not detect the compromise. No water-sector victim has been reported; Connect Secure is a common front door for utility staff and vendor remote access (editorial assessment). - Ivanti advisory and Volexity report, 13 Oct 2026 (primary); CISA KEV; CyberScoop, SecurityWeek and Cybersecurity Dive coverage, 13–14 Oct 2026 - Exploited from early Oct 2026; KEV 13 Oct 2026, deadline 16 Oct 2026; third fix still pending as of 23 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Citrix NetScaler: a fourth critical flaw follows three exploited ones, and builds that fixed September’s zero-days need upgrading again
item.category: Advisory — Three exploited NetScaler flaws in CISA KEV and a fourth critical SAML flaw; remote-access edge
item.description: Citrix disclosed CVE-2026-107406 on 8 October (bulletin CTX697191), a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider, rated CVSS v4.0 9.5. Citrix says it may allow code execution or denial of service and knows of no exploitation; it was still not in KEV as of CISA’s 21 October catalog. Builds that fixed the late-September zero-days stay exposed when used as a SAML identity provider, and CISA urged customers to patch on 9 October. The earlier trio is exploited and in KEV: CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (added 27 September) and CVE-2026-88779 (added 4 October), which Citrix and watchTowr describe as a crash bug and which CISA says attackers use to force reboots so that code planted through CVE-2026-88771 runs. Google’s threat intelligence group counts dozens of affected organizations and Arctic Wolf at least 78 targeted; Shadowserver saw more than 20,000 exposed instances in late September. WaterISAC alerted members on 28 September, and no water-sector victim has been reported. NetScaler often fronts VPN and vendor access into utility networks (editorial assessment). - Citrix bulletins CTX697174 and CTX697191 (8 Oct 2026); CISA KEV and CISA patch alert, 9 Oct 2026; GTIG, Arctic Wolf, watchTowr and Shadowserver via Cybersecurity Dive and SecurityWeek; WaterISAC notification, 28 Sep 2026 - KEV additions 27 Sep and 4 Oct 2026; fourth flaw disclosed 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Siemens Software Center: attackers abuse a DLL-loading flaw in a ClickFix malware campaign, and CISA adds it to KEV
item.category: Advisory — Exploited flaw in a Siemens Windows application, CISA KEV; abused in a ClickFix malware campaign
item.description: Siemens confirmed on 19 October that CVE-2026-110936, an uncontrolled search-path flaw in its Siemens Software Center Windows application, is being exploited. Attackers bundle a genuine, validly signed copy of the program with their own DLLs, so the trusted Siemens binary loads their code; Siemens ties the activity to the “Romulus” ClickFix campaign, which lures users into running the files themselves, and says no Siemens system, product or update channel was breached to its knowledge. It names no final malware. Siemens rates the flaw CVSS v3.1 6.7 / v4.0 8.4 and fixed it in V4.0.9.8; existing installations update automatically on next start. CISA added it to KEV on 20 October with a 3 November federal deadline and republished the advisory as ICSA-26-295-03 on 22 October. In our assessment, the risk for utilities sits on engineering and SCADA workstations: application-allowlisting rules that trust anything Siemens-signed would let such a bundle run. - Siemens ProductCERT exploitation notice, 19 Oct 2026, and SSA-580366 (primary); CISA KEV, 20 Oct 2026; CISA ICSA-26-295-03, 22 Oct 2026; SecurityWeek, 19 Oct 2026 - Advisory 15 Oct 2026; exploitation confirmed 19 Oct; KEV 20 Oct; CISA republication 22 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] PHP2Shell reaches OT products: Schneider, ABB and Moxa issue notices, and one Schneider engineering tool has no fix yet
item.category: Advisory — Critical PHP flaws under mass exploitation attempts reach OT vendor products; one Schneider tool has no fix
item.description: Two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (“PHP2Shell”, each rated CVSS v4.0 9.2 by the PHP security team), were fixed on 21 October in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Amazon says exploit attempts began on 17 October, four days before the fixes, and attempts have since run into the millions; researchers mostly see scanning and non-working exploits, and no confirmed successful compromise has been reported. The flaws are not in KEV. On 22 October Schneider Electric published SESB-2026-295-01: EcoStruxure Security Expert is fixed in 1.48.4.0, ProLeiT LINEoptimize users get remediation through ProLeiT support, and EcoStruxure Control Engineering has no fix yet while Schneider prepares a remediation plan. ABB (APROL, SA26P015) and Moxa (MPSA-260001) have also published notices. In our assessment, the larger exposure for most utilities is ordinary PHP: websites and customer-payment portals, often run by an outside provider. - Schneider Electric SESB-2026-295-01, 22 Oct 2026 (primary); ABB SA26P015 and Moxa MPSA-260001 notice listings; BleepingComputer (Amazon findings), 22 Oct 2026; The Hacker News, 23 Oct 2026 - PHP fixes 21 Oct 2026; attempts since 17 Oct; vendor notices 22–23 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] A FortiManager breach at a managed service provider exposed settings for 500-plus client firewalls; the FortiOS flaw used to gain root is now in KEV
item.category: Advisory — Exploited FortiOS flaw in CISA KEV; FortiManager-to-FortiGate compromise at a managed service provider
item.description: Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 reported on 14 October that attackers broke into a telecommunications managed service provider through its FortiManager, using the 2024 “FortiJump” flaw CVE-2024-47575, then used CVE-2025-61624, a FortiOS command-line path-traversal flaw, to get root on managed FortiGate firewalls and plant a loader Unit 42 calls PEERSTITCH. The stolen archive held configuration data for more than 500 FortiGates protecting the provider and its clients; Unit 42 calls that exposure of configuration and credential material, not confirmed intrusion into the client networks. It tracks the cluster as CL-STA-0954 (also UNC5820) and names no state. Fortinet fixed CVE-2025-61624 in April, rates it Medium and says it needs privileged, authenticated access; CISA added it to KEV on 16 October with a 19 October deadline. The CVE record lists Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808, which runs FortiOS, among affected products. Many small utilities have their firewalls managed by an outside provider (editorial assessment). - Unit 42 report, 14 Oct 2026 (primary); Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-122; CISA KEV, 16 Oct 2026; The Hacker News, 16 Oct 2026 - Flaw fixed Apr 2026; report 14 Oct 2026; KEV 16 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] MikroTik RouterOS: three flaws now in CISA KEV, and a new pre-authentication CVSS 9.8 bug in a 29 September CISA advisory
item.category: Advisory — Confirmed exploited router flaw chain, CISA KEV; new unexploited pre-auth flaw
item.description: CISA’s exploited list now holds three RouterOS flaws: CVE-2026-86060 and CVE-2026-67277, added 10 September, and CVE-2026-67279, an authentication bypass added 25 September with a 28 September federal deadline. Chained with CVE-2026-86060, CVE-2026-67279 lets an attacker take administrative control of an internet-exposed router without a password; CERT Polska corrected the chain on 22 September, so earlier reports that named other CVE IDs in it were wrong. Fixes came on 3 September in RouterOS 7.24.2, 7.23.4 and 6.49.21, and exploitation is reported from as early as 2 September. Separately, CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-06 (29 September, updated 30 September) covers CVE-2026-84411, an integer underflow in HTTP request handling that is reachable before login and could allow remote code execution or a crash, rated CVSS v3.1 9.8. CISA lists every RouterOS version below 7.24 as affected and reports no known exploitation; it is not in KEV. MikroTik routers are widely used at small utilities’ remote sites and as cellular or VPN gateways (editorial assessment). - CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-06, 29 Sep 2026, updated 30 Sep 2026; CISA KEV listings via The Hacker News; CERT Polska correction, 22 Sep 2026 - KEV additions 10 and 25 Sep 2026; CISA ICS advisory 29 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] FortiMail and Cisco SD-WAN Manager zero-days join CISA’s exploited list; Fortinet now lists fixed releases
item.category: Advisory — Two more exploited edge zero-days in CISA KEV: FortiMail and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
item.description: Two more internet-facing products were confirmed exploited at the turn of the month. Fortinet advisory FG-IR-26-175, published 1 October, covers CVE-2026-104286 (CVSS 9.8), a path-traversal flaw in the web interface of FortiMail’s identity-based encryption feature that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files on the system. Fortinet says it has been reported exploited in the wild, and CISA added it to KEV on 1 October with a 4 October deadline. Fortinet’s 5 October update lists fixed releases 7.4.9, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2; the 7.2 branch must move to 7.4 or later. Cisco disclosed on 30 September that CVE-2026-76504 (CVSS 9.8) in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager lets a remote attacker bypass an authentication rule on an API endpoint and gain administrator access; Cisco says it saw active exploitation in September, CISA listed it the same day with a 3 October deadline, and Cisco revised its advisory on 2 October. Neither vendor has named an actor or victims. In our assessment, FortiMail sits in the corporate mail path that utility staff and vendors rely on, and an SD-WAN manager can control the links to treatment plants and remote pumping sites. - Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-175, 1 Oct 2026, updated 5 Oct 2026; Cisco advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-webauth-xr8beuuU, 30 Sep 2026, revised 2 Oct 2026; CISA KEV - KEV additions 30 Sep and 1 Oct 2026; Fortinet fixed releases listed 5 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] October OT patches: Siemens S7-1500 web-server flaws have no fix yet; Schneider Sage RTUs and Ignition get updates
item.category: Advisory — October OT patch cycle: Siemens S7-1500, Schneider Sage RTU, Inductive Automation Ignition; no known exploitation
item.description: Siemens’ 13 October release includes SSA-591731, eight web-server flaws in S7-1500, ET 200SP, ET 200pro and Drive Controller CPUs, rated up to CVSS v3.1 9.6 (v4.0 9.4), that could let an attacker run code in a logged-in user’s browser and carry out PLC operations with that user’s rights. All versions are affected and only mitigations are available so far. A separate advisory, SSA-784472, lists 377 flaws in the optional Linux subsystem of the S7-1500 TM MFP module, also without a fix. Schneider Electric’s SEVD-2026-286-02 covers Sage RTUs (1410, 1430, 1450, 2400, 3030 Magnum and 4400) that do not properly verify firmware, so a modified image could be loaded when an administrator runs an update (CVE-2026-102250, CVSS v3.1 7.2 / v4.0 8.6); firmware C3414-500-S02L0 fixes it. CISA also flagged an Ignition SCADA privilege-escalation flaw, CVE-2026-92817 (CVSS v3.1 8.8), fixed in 8.1.55 and 8.3.9. CISA republished Siemens’ 13 October advisories on 22 October (ICSA-26-295-02 to -18), and the S7 web-server and TM MFP issues still had no fix. None is known to be exploited or listed in KEV. S7-1500 PLCs, Sage RTUs and Ignition all turn up in water and wastewater SCADA (editorial assessment). - Siemens ProductCERT SSA-591731 and SSA-784472; Schneider Electric SEVD-2026-286-02; CISA ICSA-26-286-01 (Ignition), all 13 Oct 2026 (primary); SecurityWeek ICS Patch Tuesday roundup, 14 Oct 2026; CISA republications ICSA-26-295-02 to -18, 22 Oct 2026 - Published 13 Oct 2026; CISA republished 22 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Mitsubishi Electric fixes an authentication bypass in ICONICS GENESIS64 and GENESIS; MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz get no fix
item.category: Advisory — Critical-rated authentication bypass in ICONICS SCADA, HMI and historian software; no fix for three older products
item.description: Mitsubishi Electric advisory 2026-006, published 15 October, covers flaws across its ICONICS SCADA, HMI and historian products. The most serious, CVE-2026-16436 (CVSS v4.0 9.2), is a shared, fixed challenge-response that can unlock any user account; a remote attacker must first obtain the challenge response. CVE-2026-16438 (v4.0 9.4) grants default DCOM permissions to the administrator account, and the advisory also lists a challenge-file permissions flaw and the older libwebp bug CVE-2023-4863. Affected are GENESIS up to 11.03 and GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI and IoTWorX up to 10.97.3; ICONICS Suite and IoTWorX 10.98 and GENESIS 11.04 fix them. MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz, all versions, will get no fix, and Mitsubishi advises migrating or applying mitigations. No exploitation is reported and none of the flaws is in KEV. GENESIS64 runs SCADA and HMI screens in water and wastewater, among other sectors (editorial assessment). - Mitsubishi Electric PSIRT advisory 2026-006, 15 Oct 2026 (primary) - Published 15 Oct 2026; no CISA republication found in the 20 or 22 Oct batches

item.title: [High] CISA flags WAGO controller and Moxa edge-gateway flaws, both listing water and wastewater: a low-privilege command injection to root and a hard-coded key
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICS advisories for controller and edge-gateway firmware; Water and Wastewater listed; no known exploitation
item.description: CISA’s 20 October batch includes two advisories that name Water and Wastewater Systems among the affected sectors. ICSA-26-293-02 republishes CERT@VDE’s VDE-2026-096 for WAGO CC100, PFC100 G2, PFC200 G2, TP600, Edge Controller and WP400 devices on firmware older than 4.10.0 (FW32). CVE-2026-80466 (CVSS v3.1 8.8) lets a logged-in, low-privileged user inject operating-system commands through routing settings in the web-based management interface, which a root helper then runs; CVE-2026-88850 (v3.1 8.1) lets low-privileged users change root-owned PROFIBUS settings. Firmware 4.10.0 (FW32) fixes both. ICSA-26-293-03 covers Moxa AIG-302 ThingsPro Edge gateways up to firmware 1.4.0: CVE-2026-109813, a hard-coded cryptographic key (v3.1 8.1 / v4.0 8.6), and a missing-authorization flaw, CVE-2026-109812 (v3.1 6.8 / v4.0 6.9); version 1.4.1 fixes both. Neither advisory reports exploitation, and neither is in KEV. Controllers and gateways like these often sit in pump-station and telemetry panels (editorial assessment). - CISA ICSA-26-293-02 (WAGO, republishing CERT@VDE VDE-2026-096) and ICSA-26-293-03 (Moxa, MPSA-262560), 20 Oct 2026, via the CIRCL vulnerability database (primary) - Published 20 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] CISA flags open-source code inside OT products: an lwIP SMTP-client overflow rated 9.8 and six Eclipse Milo OPC UA flaws
item.category: Advisory — Flaws in two open-source components used inside OT products; CISA lists water and wastewater
item.description: Two CISA advisories this month name Water and Wastewater Systems among the affected sectors for flaws in widely reused open-source code. ICSA-26-279-02 (6 October) covers CVE-2026-15340, a buffer overflow in the SMTP client of the lwIP embedded TCP/IP stack, version 2.2.1, rated CVSS v3.1 9.8; it is fixed by an upstream patch rather than a new release, and real-world exposure depends on whether a device maker uses lwIP’s SMTP client at all. ICSA-26-288-01 (15 October) covers six flaws in Eclipse Milo, a Java OPC UA client and server library, the highest rated CVSS v3.1 8.2; version 1.1.5 fixes them, and the older 0.6.x line will get no fix. Neither is in KEV, and no exploitation has been reported. The practical exposure sits in the products that embed these components, which makes this a question for your SCADA, telemetry and instrument vendors (editorial assessment). - CISA ICSA-26-279-02, 6 Oct 2026, and ICSA-26-288-01, 15 Oct 2026, via the CIRCL vulnerability database (primary) - Published 6 and 15 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] Lantronix G520 cellular gateway flaws could let an attacker swap firmware and run code as root
item.category: Advisory — Cellular gateway firmware-signing flaw; CISA lists water and wastewater, no known exploitation
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-01, released 29 September, covers two flaws in Lantronix G520 Series cellular gateways running firmware 2.6.0.4R6_stable: CVE-2026-91191, improper verification of a cryptographic signature, and CVE-2026-84409, a cross-site scripting bug, each rated CVSS v3.1 7.5 (v4 7.7). CISA says exploitation could let an attacker replace the device software and execute arbitrary code with root privileges. It lists Water and Wastewater Systems among the affected sectors, alongside Energy and Transportation Systems, and says the product is deployed worldwide. Firmware 2.6.0.7R6 fixes both, and no known public exploitation has been reported to CISA. Cellular gateways like this often connect lift stations, tanks and other unstaffed sites to SCADA, so a compromised unit sits directly on the control path (editorial assessment). - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-272-01, 29 Sep 2026 (primary) - Released 29 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] Accenture, Dragos and SANS launch a foundation offering free OT monitoring, deployment and training to up to 500 small utilities, water and wastewater included
item.category: Regulation & Policy — Industry-funded OT security programme for small utilities
item.description: Accenture, Dragos and the SANS Institute announced the Community Cyber Resilience Foundation on 20 October: a nonprofit with about $10 million in initial funding and services, with technology support from Elastic. Its first phase covers up to 500 utilities with annual revenue under $100 million, a threshold the companies say covers 97% of utilities, on top of the more than 100 already in Dragos’s Community Defense Program. The foundation’s site lists water, wastewater, electric and natural-gas utilities in the US and Canada; Dragos’s announcement refers to US utilities. Members get the Dragos Platform, Neighborhood Keeper and OT-CERT; assessment, deployment and ongoing support from Accenture; SANS training with GIAC certification; and hardware funding where needed. Enrollment “opens soon” and an interest list is open now. There is no government involvement. In our assessment, this removes the cost barrier for small systems that have never had OT network monitoring; finding staff time to act on it is the harder part. - Dragos announcement, 20 Oct 2026 (primary); Community Cyber Resilience Foundation website; The Record and Industrial Cyber, 21 Oct 2026 - Announced 20 Oct 2026; enrollment not yet open

item.title: [Info] CISA’s final cyber incident-reporting rule reaches White House review; text and start dates are not yet public
item.category: Regulation & Policy — Federal cyber incident-reporting rule (CIRCIA)
item.description: The White House Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs logged receipt of CISA’s final rule under the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act (RIN 1670-AA04) on 1 October, and the review is pending. The statute set an October 2025 deadline, and CISA’s later targets of May and September 2026 slipped; HIPAA Journal reports publication is expected before year-end. The law calls for covered entities to report covered cyber incidents within 72 hours and ransom payments within 24 hours, but no obligation applies until the final rule sets its dates. The rule text, including which water and wastewater systems it covers, is not public, and the review can still change it. No final rule had been published as of 23 October. - OIRA regulatory review record (reginfo.gov), received 1 Oct 2026 (primary); HIPAA Journal, 5 Oct 2026; Paubox, 8 and 14 Oct 2026 - Under review since 1 Oct 2026; not published as of 23 Oct 2026
